findings.where: the arriving sheet, whole animation (frames 16-162 and the repeat at 179-325); measured at frame 46 and frame 325
findings.what: The sheet that unfolds is a machine-cut rectangle, not a torn one: at frame 46 its left edge occupies a single column over 90 rows (std 0.00 px), and at frame 325 its top edge is exactly row 1074 and its bottom exactly row 1503 for all 580 columns measured (std 0.00 px and 0.49 px), while the other sheets in the same frames have top edges that wander 22.25-34.94 px.
findings.why: The rubric judges this row in slow motion on this clip; a sheet whose silhouette is straight to a hundredth of a pixel reads as an approximation of paper rather than as photographed torn stock.

findings.where: the fold face and its crease, frame 46, x 120-700, y 1350-1560
findings.what: The fold is a one-dimensional gradient painted on a flat plane: the median per-row standard deviation ACROSS the sheet's 580-px width is 1.50 grey levels, the vertical profile is the same to within 2 grey at x=100, 200, 400, 600 and 700 (plateau 178.5, crease trough 111-116, second plateau 157-166, step to 236), and the crease is a 20.5-grey step in one pixel row at y=1429.
findings.why: 'Blender-rendered folds and creases under one consistent light direction' requires shading that changes along the fold as the surface turns; shading that is constant along its whole length is a flat image being transformed, which the rubric names as the failure.

findings.where: the cast shadow under the arriving sheet, frame 325 at x=400 (vertical) and y=1560 (horizontal); frame 46 at y=1500
findings.what: The cast shadow is a hard slab, not a contact shadow: at x=400 it goes 247.8 -> 108.0 -> 30.0 grey across four rows (y 1501-1505), then sits flat at 30-37 grey for the next 60 px; its right boundary at y=1560 steps 35 -> 74.9 -> 94.9 -> 103.9 over about 12 px; at frame 46 the equivalent step is 228.0 -> 40.0 in five pixels.
findings.why: 'Contact shadows baked from the render's own lighting rather than applied as a uniform blur' - a hard-edged uniform slab of the sheet's own silhouette is neither baked nor even blurred.

findings.where: the folding sheet's surface vs a settled note in the same frame, frame 46 (flattest 48-px blank patches, high-pass at sigma 3)
findings.what: The unfolding sheet carries almost no stock: 0.90 grey levels of micro-texture against 4.56 on the settled torn note directly above it in the same frame, a 5.1x deficit measured the same way; the paper only acquires tooth after it lands.
findings.why: 'Real scanned stock' has to be present while the sheet is the subject of the shot, not applied once the animation is over.

findings.where: the five module cards (DATES, TO DO, DATES THAT MATTER, RITUALS, THE SHELF); TO DO measured at y 737-900, x 400-1072
findings.what: Every module card is a machine-cut plate on a uniform blurred drop shadow: top/bottom edge roughness 0.00-0.81 px over 660 columns, TO DO exactly 673x164 px with 0.00 px roughness on all four sides, and its shadow is a constant band (mean 74.14 grey at 2 px below the edge rising monotonically to 93.75 at 26 px, with a column-to-column spread of 8.18 grey that is SMALLER than the bare wood's own 14.93) - the shadow flattens the grain instead of being shaped by anything. The torn strips on the same screen wander 6.61-9.36 px.
findings.why: A rectangle with a uniform blurred drop shadow standing in for a paper surface is the fourth anti-goal and is exactly the 'applied as a uniform blur' the rubric excludes.

findings.where: the last sheet in the list ('medium, and extremely involved'), bottom edge at y=2627->2628, x 157-1202
findings.what: The sheet is sliced by a straight machine cut with no shadow: 94.5% of its columns end at the same row, the transition is 233.04 -> 94.64 grey (138.4 levels) in a single un-antialiased pixel row across 804-1046 columns, and the desk 2-5 px beneath reads 94.64 against 94.61 twelve pixels further away - a 0.03-grey difference, where every other sheet on this screen carries a shadow about 40 grey deep. The same straight cut appears at y=281 (459 px) at the top of the same list, at y=281 (670 px) on 13_messenger_states.png, y=736 and y=900 on 03_us.png, y=2942 on 05_settings.png and y=1462 on 12_search.png.
findings.why: Paper cannot end in a razor-straight, un-antialiased line with no contact shadow; the scroll viewport is cutting the sheet, and the cut is visible on the hero the rubric names as its first judging site.

findings.where: on the wood in the gaps between sheets; e.g. 02_chat.png y=650 x 962-1215, y=316 x 586-770, y=341 x 965-1130
findings.what: One-pixel bright rules are drawn across the desk: at 02_chat y=650, x=1100 three consecutive rows read 78.9 / 127.3 / 80.2, a +48-grey spike one pixel tall running 254 px; at y=316, x=680 they read 105.9 / 141.1 / 105.2. Nine of the ten stills carry them - 12_search.png has 33 such rows, the longest 440 px, at a mean ridge of +34.9 grey; 03_us.png 21 rows, 04_moments.png 17, 13_messenger_states.png 12.
findings.why: A photograph of wood contains no one-pixel line; these are element borders showing through and they announce the ground under the paper as drawn rather than photographed.

findings.where: the desk, 80 clean 64-px windows at least 12 px from any sheet, compared with 80 equivalent windows of blank paper
findings.what: The desk has no cross-grain structure at all: its mean absolute horizontal gradient is 5.58x its vertical one (2.562 vs 0.459), i.e. all of its texture is one-directional bands, while the paper measures 0.52 (0.841 vs 1.607) - near-isotropic, with a visibly fibrous, speckled high-pass. The desk shows no tile repeat (max horizontal autocorrelation 0.21 across four full-width bands), so it is not tiled; it is painted.
findings.why: The paper is the surface the row is about and it holds up, but it is laid on a ground that is plainly not a photograph, and the two read against each other at 300 per cent.

findings.where: the four cursive notes (y 287-641, 925-1232, 1712-2088, 2406-2628), 158 ink marks
findings.what: Repeated glyphs repeat exactly: 14 of 158 marks (8.9%) have another mark on the same screen matching at normalized cross-correlation >= 0.99 under translation alone (no rescaling), and 84 (53.2%) at >= 0.97; the seven pairs I inspected at >= 0.99 - o/o at (254,992) and (865,1001) r=0.998, t/t r=0.997, g/g r=0.996, e/e r=0.994 twice, r/r r=0.994, o/o r=0.992 - are visually indistinguishable.
findings.why: 'Handwriting with multiple variants per glyph' - variants do exist and are visible (the two instances of 'dog' in the fifth note differ in d, o and g), but the cycle is short enough that identical twins sit a line or two apart.

findings.where: the ink of every mark on the four cursive notes
findings.what: Pressure lives in the outline only: within a mark the stroke width varies well (median coefficient of variation 0.305 over 157 marks, p90-p10 = 0.72 of the mean width) but the core darkness of a mark varies by only 3.52 grey levels - the ink is a flat fill.
findings.why: 'Real pressure variance' in a pen is width and density together; half of it is missing.

findings.where: the boxes logs/crops.json records: hand 805,2540-1225,2800 and edge 518,2596-938,2856
findings.what: The 300 per cent crop the rubric names for judging the hand is mostly tear and desk with one partial word of script across its top edge, and the 'edge' crop lands on the composer's 'write something' placeholder rather than on a message; I had to cut my own 300 per cent crops over the handwriting to judge this row.
findings.why: The rubric says the hand is judged at three hundred per cent on the Chat hero, and the crops supplied do not put the hand there.

findings.what: Thirteen of the fifteen present artifacts predate the capture that began at 2026-09-08T06:05:04Z - 06_unfolding.mp4 among them, written 00:11:52Z - and only 02_chat.png and 11_chat_scroll.mp4 were written by this run; 09_two_devices.png and 16_setup_android.png were not captured at all.
findings.why: The clip the rubric names as one of its two judging sites is a clip of an older build, so nothing in the fold findings above can be checked against the build the hero shows.

what_is_working: The paper itself is photographed, not simulated. On 02_chat.png the flattest blank 80-px patches of six different notes carry 3.84-4.15 grey levels of high-pass texture with a fibrous, speckled, near-isotropic character (mean |dx|/|dy| = 0.52), and a contrast-stretched view of the residual shows short strand-like marks and specks rather than smooth blobs.

The stock does not tile and is not one scan reused. Along a 1080-px blank band of the top note the high-pass autocorrelates at most 0.18 beyond lag 20; a 64x64 texture block taken from the fifth note template-matches into the first note's blank band at only NCC 0.45 and into the composer's at 0.28.

Tear masks do not repeat on a single screen. The eight notes' top-edge profiles on 02_chat.png, detrended and normalised, cross-correlate at most |r| = 0.632 over all lags (a duplicate mask would be ~0.99), and no edge repeats within itself beyond |r| = 0.58; two sheets I compared directly on a scroll frame are visibly different fibre for fibre. This is independently what logs/tears.json reports (8 visible, 8 distinct, repeats {}).

One consistent light direction across the still. Pooled desk luminance by distance from the sheets on 02_chat.png: below the sheets the median falls to 60.7 at 4 px against 100.6 far away, and to the right to 64.6 at 12 px against 95.7; above (101.5 -> 103.5) and to the left (100.6 -> 105.5) there is no dip at all. Light from the upper left, shadows down and right - and the rendered feeling objects on 01_pulse.png and 07_feeling_landing.mp4 are lit from the same quarter with their shadows falling the same way.

The still's contact shadows are not a rigid offset of the silhouette. Below the fifth note the gap between the sheet's own edge and the outer boundary of the dark band varies with a standard deviation of 15.7 px about a mean of 21.4 px, and the two profiles correlate at only r = 0.643 at every lag.

The tear edges at 300 per cent carry real deckle: light fibres standing off the sheet into the desk with dark pockets beneath them, and the fibre band is a genuine mix (41.6% of the 6-px band outside the sheets is darker than the open desk, 9% near black, the rest lighter) rather than a uniform drawn outline.

Feelings are physical objects, not icons: the candle-like form on 01_pulse.png and 07_feeling_landing.mp4, the wrapped sweet, the folded-paper forms and the amber arc on 15_authored_feeling.mp4 are rendered geometry with cast shadows, faceting and their own material.
verdict: The paper on the Chat hero is genuinely photographed and I could not break it: the stock carries fibrous scan grain at 3.8-4.2 grey levels that neither tiles (max autocorrelation 0.18) nor repeats between notes (best block match NCC 0.45), the eight tear masks on the screen are all distinct (peak cross-correlation 0.63 where a duplicate would be 0.99), the light is unambiguously from the upper left with shadows below and to the right and none above or left, and the shadow is not a rigid translated silhouette (edge-to-shadow gap varying by 15.7 px, correlation 0.64). The handwriting has real width modulation and visible variants. That is most of the row, and it is well done. But the row is judged in two places, and the second one fails outright. In 06_unfolding.mp4 the sheet that unfolds is a rectangle straight to 0.00 px on every edge for the whole animation while its neighbours wander 22-35 px; it carries 0.90 grey of texture against 4.56 on the settled note beside it; its fold is a purely one-dimensional gradient whose shading is constant to 1.50 grey across the sheet's entire 580-px width, with the crease a 20.5-grey step in a single row; and its shadow is a hard slab that goes 247.8 to 30.0 grey in four pixels and then holds flat. Nothing there is rendered geometry catching light. The same flat-plate treatment governs the five module cards on 03_us.png, which are machine-cut rectangles on a uniform blurred drop shadow whose depth is constant along the whole 673-px edge. On top of that, the bottom sheet on the hero is sliced by the scroll viewport with a 138-grey step in one un-antialiased pixel row across 804 columns and no contact shadow at all beneath it, and nine of the ten stills carry one-pixel bright rules drawn across the wood (up to 440 px long, +35 grey) that no photograph of a desk could contain. Because a flat rectangle on a uniform blurred shadow is standing in for paper in the clip the rubric names, and because that clip predates the capture so it cannot even be checked against the build the hero shows, this category cannot exceed its floor. 15 of 25.
